bureau: Registros o bancos de datos de deudas (DICOM, Boletín Comercial)
note: Ley 19.628 on the protection of private life, article 18 (as replaced by Ley 19.812, the 'Ley DICOM'), read in the Superintendencia de Seguridad Social's (SUSESO) copy of the article (the Biblioteca del Congreso's own copy refuses this environment with a 401): data on a person's economic, financial, banking or commercial obligations may not be communicated once five years have passed since the obligation became due, nor once it has been paid or otherwise extinguished. Article 19, quoted in SUSESO's Dictamen 29336-2017, has the creditor tell the register within seven working days of payment. The game reads this as five years while unpaid (keep 5) and the mark lifting nine days after payment (clears 9: seven working days read as nine calendar days). The registers are named as SUSESO's dictamen names them (DICOM and the Boletín Comercial). Ley 21.719, which rewrites the data-protection law, takes effect on 1 December 2026; this file is the law in force today. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the next monthly update.

sources.title: SUSESO, Normativa y jurisprudencia: Ley 19.628, artículo 18
sources.said: Artículo 18.- En ningún caso pueden comunicarse los datos a que se refiere el artículo anterior, que se relacionen con una persona identificada o identificable, luego de transcurridos cinco años desde que la respectiva obligación se hizo exigible. Tampoco se podrá continuar comunicando los datos relativos a dicha obligación después de haber sido pagada o haberse extinguido por otro modo legal.
